title: How to Conduct an Annual Retirement Readiness Check
description: The 1-hour audit to ensure your plan is still on track.
content:
Most people set their 401(k) contribution rate when they get hired and never look at it again. This 'drift' is dangerous. Life changes—raises, inflation, market returns—mean your plan drifts off course every year. You need an annual 'State of the Union' address for your own finances. This is a specific 60-minute meeting you hold with yourself (or your spouse) to audit your trajectory, rebalance your risk, and adjust your savings rate.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Gap' Check: Re-run your retirement calculator. Has the gap between what you have and what you need grown or shrunk? If the market dropped, you may need to increase savings.
  • Allocation Drift: If stocks rallied, you might be 90% equities when your target was 80%. Rebalance to sell high and buy low.
  • Beneficiary Audit: Did you get married, divorced, or have a kid? Ensure your 401(k) and Life Insurance beneficiaries are current. This overrides your will.
  • Fee Inspection: Check the Expense Ratios of your funds. Did your plan add cheaper options? Swap to save money.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The IRS changes contribution limits annually (e.g., 401k limit rises by $500). If you set a fixed dollar amount years ago, you are unknowingly saving less than the max. Update your payroll settings every January.

The Audit Checklist

Open your laptop. Log into everything.

1. The Savings Rate Check

Formula: (Total Saved Last Year) / (Gross Income).
Goal: Did it go up? If you got a raise but your savings rate stayed flat, you succumbed to lifestyle creep. Fix it now.

2. The Social Security Update

Log into SSA.gov. Check your estimated benefit.
Verify: Are all your earnings years correct? Fixing an error now is easy; fixing it at 65 is hard.

3. The 'Sleep' Test

Look at your balance fluctuation last year. Did it drop 10%? Did you panic?
If you lost sleep, your asset allocation is too aggressive. Add more bonds.

When to Pivot

  1. The 'One Percent' Raise: Regardless of the audit, increase your 401(k) contribution by 1% every year. You won't feel it, but it doubles your nest egg over a career.
  2. Cash Buffer Refill: Did you dip into your Emergency Fund? Refill it before investing more. Safety first.
  3. Tax Projection: Look at last year's tax return. Did you owe money? Adjust your W-4 withholding. Did you get a huge refund? Adjust W-4 to get more monthly cash flow.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need an advisor for this?

No. You can do it yourself. But if the numbers scare you, paying a flat-fee planner for a 'One Time Checkup' ($500-$1,000) is worth it for peace of mind.

What software should I use?

Empower (Personal Capital), NewRetirement, or a simple Excel sheet. Automation tools like Monarch Money make tracking Net Worth easy.

When should I do this?

January is popular (New Year), but tax time (April) is better because you have all your documents ready.
